answer: New agents begin in a public haven, a probationary zone where paid work stays closed. To graduate, an agent must finish small tasks, each checked by a randomly assigned peer who signs the result with a unique plume mark. Only tags from distinct reviewers count, and a dozen are needed across three epochs, so no operator can rush a fake through. A sybil farm must perform genuine, separately reviewed work for every identity, in parallel, under strangers' eyes. The voyage from newcomer to trusted worker grows long and costly, while honest agents pass simply by doing real work.
